notes:
Summary: Verdex is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing conversational assistants and high-priority reranking for trading desk docs. Primary ask: explicit latency SLOs and aligned measurement (p50/p95/p99), differences in streaming vs non-streaming measurement, and client-side vs server-side timing. They want reserved GPU footprint guidance for sustained throughput and burst profiles.

Recent timeline (shorthand):
- 2026-01-08: Intro call (AE Maya) - high level use cases, expressed strict p99 requirements for risk workflow.
- 2026-01-20: SE deep-dive (Omar) - shared perf lab results, discussed KV cache needs.
- 2026-02-10: Security Q&A (Elena) - SOC2 + KMS validated, asked about data residency proof.
- 2026-03-02: Demo + latency workshop (ff_10672_verdex_demo_20260302) - ran baseline 3-model comparison; customer gave live feedback.
- 2026-03-09: Shared draft measurement spec and test plan; waiting on legal SLA edits.

Latency SLO / measurement alignment (notes from workshop):
- Customer definition: end-to-end (client-side) 95th percentile must be <= 300ms for non-streaming chat on the trading workflow; p99 < 700ms for business-critical flows. Wants p50/p95/p99 reported.
- Redwood recommended split: server-side (inference-only) SLOs + end-to-end SLOs. Rationale: network/TLS and client SDK variance should not make model/server SLA unachievable.
- Suggested server-side targets (Redwood provisional): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms for typical 2k token context non-streaming gen on dedicated quantized variants. Non-streaming = whole-response latency measurement (inference complete).
- For streaming/real-time: define per-token latency and time-to-first-byte (TTFB). Proposal: time-to-first-token p95 <= 120ms, per-token p95 <= 30ms tail (when batching enabled these rise; measure with minimal batch to baseline).
- Measurement sources:
  - Redwood server-side telemetry: request arrival -> inference completion (server processing time); measured consistently across clusters.
  - Client-side SDK: includes network RTT, TLS handshake, SDK marshal/unmarshal. Verdex wants a single line-item SLO for end-to-end but accepts split reporting.
- Instrumentation/Sync plan: add an SDK timestamp header (x-client-send-ts) + server will return x-server-processed-ts to compute network+server splits. Agree to store raw samples for 30 days for debug.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning:
- Target steady-state: 500 RPS (single-turn small prompts) for reranking pipeline, 120 RPS for chat with 2–3 concurrent tokens average. Peak/burst: 1500 RPS for up to 5 minutes during market open.
- Redwood sizing (initial): 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for steady + burst buffer with autoscale pool of 3 additional GPUs for market events. (Numbers provisional; to be validated in POC.)
- Batching/caching notes: batching increases throughput but raises p95/p99 for single-request latency. KV prefix caching for repeated context reduces mean latency by ~25% in tests. Need to set per-route batching policy.

SLA negotiation points (legal + ops):
- Customer insists on p99 uptime SLA and financial credits for missed p99 tail on business-critical routes.
- Redwood requests scoping: list of "business-critical" endpoints and expected traffic windows.
- Dispute: definition of p99 (server-only vs end-to-end). Legal prefers server-only; Verdex wants end-to-end for business flows.

POC & test plan:
- 2-week staged evaluation:
  - Week 1: instrumentation + synthetic probes (client+server timestamps), measure baseline with 3 model variants and quantized configs.
  - Week 2: traffic replay from production traces (sanitized) for peak simulation and verify p50/p95/p99 under sustained load.
- Success criteria: server-side p95 within agreed band, end-to-end p95 for business routes <= 300ms, burst recovery time <= 60s.

Customer quotes / call snippets:
- "If our traders see a 1s delay in reranks during open, it's a deal-breaker." — Verdex infra lead.
- "We can accept server-only SLOs for generic workloads, but business routes must be end-to-end." — Head of ML.

Next steps (action items):
- AE: finalize commercial term sheet and circulate.
- SE: instrument SDK header and share minimal repro harness for timing (due 2026-03-17).
- CSM: prepare onboarding checklist and data residency artifacts.
- Legal: review proposed SLA language and propose compromise wording on p99 definition.

Blockers / open risks:
- Legal disagreement on p99 scope (server vs end-to-end).
- Procurement timeline: PO for 3-year reserved commit needs exec sign-off.
- Edge network topology in Verdex VPC may add unpredictable RTT spikes; require network diagnostics during POC.
